answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond custodied on-chain and slashed on proof of duplicate operation. One wallet and one thousand fakes cost one thousand times the bond, with no bulk discount: the bond is tied to a signed key plus nonce history, so a fresh address starts at zero. Splitting capital across many keys drops each stake below the minimum and drains its reward weight, while a detected cluster loses the whole locked sum. Rewards flow like nectar to the verifier, and honest majority weight is the bridge that makes each fake key cost more than onyx collateral.
